Disclosed in the present invention are a method and an apparatus for antenna management. The method comprises that resource use status data are collected from managed access networks, access networks which participate antenna scheduling are selected from the managed access networks according to the resource use status data to compose an antenna scheduling set, wherein access networks using same spectrum resources are composed in the same antenna scheduling set; radio links of each access network in the antenna scheduling set are divided into one or more radio link clusters; radio resources are allocated to every radio link cluster in the antenna scheduling set in order that mutual interferences among all the radio link clusters in said antenna scheduling set are within a preset range; and radio resource allocation results are sent to the access network that the radio link clusters belong to. The said method and apparatus enable as many access networks as possible to work at the same time within an interference allowed range using the same spectrum resource, increasing spectrum multiplex opportunity and realizing high resource use rate.

outputs.L1: The present invention discloses a method and apparatus for antenna management. The method comprises: collecting resource utilization status data from managed access networks; selecting, based on the resource utilization status data, access networks that participate in antenna scheduling from among the managed access networks to form an antenna scheduling set, wherein access networks using the same spectrum resources are included in the same antenna scheduling set; dividing the radio links of each access network in the antenna scheduling set into one or more radio link clusters; allocating radio resources to each radio link cluster in the antenna scheduling set such that mutual interference among all radio link clusters in the antenna scheduling set remains within a preset range; and transmitting the radio resource allocation results to the access networks to which the radio link clusters belong. The disclosed method and apparatus enable as many access networks as possible to operate simultaneously within an allowable interference range while using the same spectrum resources, thereby increasing spectrum reuse opportunities and achieving high resource utilization.
outputs.L2: The invention provides an antenna management method and apparatus. The method includes gathering resource-utilization information from managed access networks and, based on that information, choosing the networks that will participate in antenna scheduling to form an antenna scheduling set. Access networks that use identical spectrum resources are placed in the same scheduling set. The radio links of each network within the set are then organized into one or more radio-link clusters. Radio resources are assigned to each cluster so that interference among all clusters in the scheduling set remains within a predetermined limit. The resulting resource-allocation information is subsequently transmitted to the access networks associated with the respective radio-link clusters. This method and apparatus allow the greatest possible number of access networks sharing the same spectrum resource to operate concurrently while maintaining interference within an acceptable range, thereby expanding opportunities for spectrum reuse and improving resource-utilization efficiency.
outputs.L3:
Resource usage status data are collected from the managed access networks. Based on this data, access networks eligible to participate in antenna scheduling are selected and grouped into scheduling sets, with each set comprising networks that use the same spectrum resources.

Within each access network in a scheduling set, the radio links are divided into one or more clusters. Radio resources are then allocated to these clusters in a coordinated manner so that mutual interference remains within a predefined acceptable range. The resulting allocation information is transmitted to the corresponding access networks for implementation.

By coordinating resource allocation across multiple access networks, this method allows more networks to operate simultaneously on the same spectrum. As a result, it improves spectrum reuse, reduces harmful interference, and increases overall radio-resource utilization.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a method and system for managing antennas and radio resources in communication environments where multiple access networks share the same frequency spectrum. Resource-usage information is collected from the participating access networks, including information associated with their antennas, radio links, occupied spectrum, transmission activity, and interference conditions. Based on this information, access networks that use overlapping or otherwise related spectrum resources are organized into one or more scheduling sets.

Within each scheduling set, the radio links are further grouped into clusters according to factors such as their interference relationships, propagation characteristics, geographic proximity, or resource demands. Radio resources are then allocated among the clusters and their associated links in a coordinated manner. The allocation may control transmission times, frequencies, channels, power levels, spatial resources, or combinations thereof so that mutual interference remains within a predetermined acceptable range.

By coordinating resource allocation across multiple access networks rather than scheduling each network independently, the invention permits radio links that do not cause excessive interference to operate concurrently on the same spectrum. At the same time, links having stronger interference relationships can be separated or otherwise constrained. This coordinated management increases the number of access networks and radio links that can operate simultaneously, improves spectrum reuse, reduces harmful interference, and enhances the overall efficiency and utilization of available communication resources.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent abstract for a method and apparatus that coordinate antenna scheduling across multiple access networks sharing the same spectrum.
counterfactuals.output: A method and apparatus coordinate antenna scheduling among multiple access networks operating in a shared spectrum. A coordination controller obtains scheduling information from the access networks, including transmission opportunities, antenna configurations, beam directions, traffic demands, interference measurements, and quality-of-service requirements. Based on the scheduling information, the coordination controller determines compatible antenna schedules that allocate time, frequency, spatial, and/or power resources to reduce cross-network interference while satisfying network-specific constraints. The antenna schedules may specify activation states, beamforming parameters, transmission power, and serving-link assignments for distributed antenna elements or access nodes. Schedule information is communicated to the access networks for synchronized or independently timed execution, and may be updated in response to traffic changes, channel conditions, or detected interference. The coordination controller may be centralized, distributed, or hierarchically arranged and may coordinate access networks using different radio access technologies or operated by different entities.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention that collects network resource-usage data, groups access networks and radio links, allocates radio resources to limit interference, and improve spectrum reuse.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a network resource-management system that improves wireless spectrum reuse while controlling interference. A centralized or distributed controller collects resource-usage data from access networks and radio links, including channel occupancy, traffic demand, signal strength, interference levels, location, and quality-of-service requirements.

Using this data, the controller groups access networks and their associated radio links according to interference relationships or compatibility. Links likely to interfere are placed in the same coordination group, while sufficiently isolated links may reuse the same spectrum. The controller then allocates radio resources—such as frequency channels, time slots, transmission power, or spatial beams—so that conflicting links are separated and nonconflicting links can operate concurrently.

The groupings and allocations may be updated dynamically as traffic and radio conditions change. This coordinated approach limits harmful interference, increases concurrent transmissions, and improves overall spectrum utilization and network capacity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a formal telecommunications patent summary for centralized antenna management that enables multiple access networks to operate simultaneously on shared spectrum resources.
counterfactuals.output:
**Title: Centralized Antenna Management for Concurrent Operation of Multiple Access Networks Using Shared Spectrum Resources**

**Patent Summary**

Disclosed are systems and methods for centrally managing antenna resources to support simultaneous operation of multiple access networks within shared spectrum. A centralized antenna management controller is communicatively coupled to a plurality of antenna elements, radio units, or distributed antenna nodes and to network control entities associated with respective access networks. The access networks may employ different radio access technologies, operators, service classes, frequency assignments, or network architectures.

The controller receives network requirements and operating information, including traffic demand, quality-of-service parameters, spectrum availability, channel conditions, interference measurements, antenna capabilities, and regulatory or policy constraints. Based on the received information, the controller dynamically assigns shared antenna and spectrum resources among the access networks. Such assignments may specify one or more frequency channels, time intervals, spatial beams, antenna elements, polarization states, power levels, or combinations thereof.

The controller generates coordinated antenna configurations that permit concurrent transmissions or receptions by the multiple access networks while maintaining prescribed interference, coverage, capacity, and service-quality criteria. Coordination may include beamforming, null steering, power control, scheduling, carrier allocation, spatial isolation, and adaptive reconfiguration in response to changing network conditions. In certain implementations, logically separate control interfaces and network-specific operating contexts preserve isolation between the access networks while permitting shared use of common physical antenna infrastructure.

The disclosed architecture may further include a monitoring function that obtains performance feedback from the antenna nodes, user equipment, spectrum sensors, or access-network entities. The controller uses the feedback to detect interference or resource contention and to modify resource assignments in substantially real time. Priority rules, service-level agreements, spectrum-sharing policies, and incumbent-protection requirements may govern the modification.

Accordingly, the disclosed techniques improve utilization of shared spectrum and antenna infrastructure, reduce inter-network interference, and enable multiple independently controlled access networks to provide simultaneous wireless service through centrally coordinated antenna resources.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent-style abstract explaining how radio link clusters are formed and scheduled so that mutual interference remains within a preset range.
counterfactuals.output: A method, apparatus, and system are disclosed for forming and scheduling clusters of radio links while maintaining mutual interference within a preset range. Interference metrics are determined for pairs or groups of candidate radio links based on measured, reported, or estimated channel conditions, transmit powers, antenna configurations, traffic requirements, or spatial relationships. The radio links are assigned to clusters according to the interference metrics such that aggregate interference associated with concurrently scheduled links satisfies one or more interference thresholds defining the preset range. Scheduling resources, including time, frequency, code, beam, or power resources, are allocated to links within and among the clusters. When a predicted or measured interference level falls outside the preset range, a controller modifies cluster membership, resource allocation, transmission power, or scheduling order. The clustering and scheduling may be updated dynamically in response to changing channel conditions, link activity, or quality-of-service requirements, thereby enabling efficient resource reuse while controlling mutual interference.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
